entity.name: James Cook
entity.description: The farm boy who mapped more of Earth than anyone before him. A coal-ship apprentice from Yorkshire who turned down a captaincy to join the Royal Navy, Cook led three Pacific voyages that charted New Zealand, eastern Australia, Hawaii, and Antarctica's edge. He was killed in Hawaii at 50 during a dispute over a stolen boat.

story.name: James Cook
story.description: A grocer's apprentice turns coal-ship sailor, charts the St. Lawrence for the siege of Quebec, makes first European contact with eastern Australia, and is killed in Hawaii over a stolen cutter.

moments.name: James Cook Is Born to a Scottish Farm Laborer in Yorkshire
moments.subtitle: A boy raised 8 miles from the sea would sail farther than almost anyone in history
moments.description: On 7 November 1728, James Cook was born in the village of Marton in the North Riding of Yorkshire, approximately 8 miles from the coast. His father was a Scottish farm laborer from Roxburghshire; the family later moved to Great Ayton, where the local landowner paid for young James's schooling. At 16, Cook was apprenticed to a grocer in the fishing village of Staithes, but after 18 months proved unsuited for shop work. He moved to the port town of Whitby and began a merchant navy apprenticeship hauling coal — the unglamorous start to a career that would chart more of the Pacific Ocean than any European before him.

moments.name: Cook Charts the St. Lawrence River and Enables the Siege of Quebec
moments.subtitle: A ship's master's midnight soundings help 4,000 British soldiers slip past French guns
moments.description: In 1759, during the Seven Years' War, James Cook served as master aboard HMS Pembroke and was tasked with charting the St. Lawrence River near Quebec. Working at night under threat of French fire, Cook and other masters took soundings, marked shoals, and updated charts with unprecedented accuracy — combining hydrographic and land-surveying techniques learned from army officer Samuel Holland. The detailed charts enabled General James Wolfe to transport 4,000 troops silently across the river at night for the surprise assault on the Plains of Abraham that captured Quebec from France. Cook's cartographic skill launched his career and caught the Admiralty's attention.

moments.name: Cook Sails HMS Endeavour on a Three-Year Voyage to the Pacific
moments.subtitle: A 39-year-old coal-ship veteran commands a mission to observe Venus and secretly claim new lands
moments.description: On 25 August 1768, HMS Endeavour departed England with 73 sailors, 12 marines, and naturalist Joseph Banks on a three-year expedition to the south Pacific. The publicly stated goal was to observe the 1769 transit of Venus from Tahiti; secret orders directed Cook to search for the hypothesized southern continent and claim lands for Britain. Cook, 39, had been selected over senior officers for his exceptional cartographic skills. The voyage would result in the first European charting of New Zealand's coastline, the first recorded European contact with eastern Australia, and the collection of over 30,000 plant specimens — fundamentally reshaping European knowledge of the Pacific.

moments.name: Cook Claims the East Coast of Australia for Britain
moments.subtitle: A continent inhabited for 65,000 years gets a British flag planted on its shore
moments.description: On 22 August 1770, Captain James Cook landed at Possession Island off the northeastern tip of Australia and formally claimed the entire east coast for King George III, naming it New South Wales. Cook's Endeavour had spent four months charting 2,000 miles of previously unmapped Australian coastline, nearly sinking on the Great Barrier Reef in June when the ship struck coral. The crew spent seven weeks repairing the hull at what is now Cooktown. Cook's charts and favorable reports of the land led directly to Britain's decision to establish a penal colony at Botany Bay in 1788 — the founding act of modern Australia.

moments.name: Hawaiian Warriors Kill Captain Cook in a Dispute over a Stolen Boat
moments.subtitle: The world's greatest navigator is clubbed to death on a beach at age 50
moments.description: On 14 February 1779, Captain James Cook was killed at Kealakekua Bay, Hawaii, during his third Pacific voyage. Cook had initially been received with elaborate ceremonies by Native Hawaiians, possibly coinciding with the Makahiki festival honoring the god Lono. After departing, Cook was forced to return when a storm damaged his ship's mast. Tensions escalated when Hawaiians stole a cutter, and Cook went ashore to take a chief hostage as leverage. A confrontation erupted on the beach; Cook was struck on the head and stabbed, dying in the shallows. His death ended the Age of Exploration's greatest career — three voyages covering over 200,000 miles of ocean.
